Spatial field reconstruction ​

Fit a moving field from station measurements, read it at new locations, and separate uncertainty in the field from observation noise. The example uses a gmrf term with nearest-neighbor conditioning. The space-time fields guide covers the other field terms and when each fits the data.

Data and model ​

The data are synthetic measurements on a square measured in kilometers. A positive feature moves east and a negative feature moves north. Each station has repeated measurements at each time, which help distinguish observation noise from variation in the latent field. The generating surface is an analytic function, not a draw from the fitted prior.

Synthetic dataValue
Square side (km)100
Stations24
Observation times1, 3, 6
Observations144
Position–time states72
Neighbors8
Generating noise SD0.25

neighbors selects a Gaussian conditional representation of the observed position–time pairs. Repeated rows at the same coordinates and time read the same state. The amplitude prior uses response units, the spatial length prior uses kilometers, and the temporal length prior uses the observation time unit. Project longitude and latitude into suitable planar coordinates before fitting.

brm-comparison
A station field with unknown lengths and noise
julia
function station_field_model(data=station_data())
    @brm data begin
        sigma ~ Exponential(noise_prior)
        field ~ 0 + gmrf((east, north), time; neighbors=neighbors)
        sd(field, gmrf((east, north), time)) ~ Exponential(amplitude_scale)
        length_scale(field, gmrf((east, north), time), space) ~ LogNormal(log(spatial_prior), length_prior_sd)
        length_scale(field, gmrf((east, north), time), time) ~ LogNormal(log(temporal_prior), length_prior_sd)
        y ~ Normal(field, sigma)
    end
end

stan
functions {
real brm_gmrf_vecchia_lpdf(
    vector field,
    real spatial_length,
    real temporal_length,
    matrix L,
    vector east,
    vector north,
    array[] int origin,
    array[] int item_ptr,
    array[] int item_position,
    vector item_lag,
    array[] int pattern_ptr,
    array[] int pattern_states,
    array[] int neighbor_ptr,
    array[] int neighbor,
    array[] int state_pattern,
    int M
) {
    int C = dims(L)[1];
    int P = dims(east)[1];
    int NI = dims(item_position)[1];
    int N = dims(pattern_states)[1];
    if (dims(L)[2] != C) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_lpdf: dim mismatch — `L` dim 2 (= ", dims(L)[2], ") does not match `C` (= ", C, "), inferred from `L` dim 1. `C` sizes: `L` dim 1 (= ", dims(L)[1], "), `L` dim 2 (= ", dims(L)[2], ").");
    if (dims(north)[1] != P) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_lpdf: dim mismatch — `north` dim 1 (= ", dims(north)[1], ") does not match `P` (= ", P, "), inferred from `east` dim 1. `P` sizes: `east` dim 1 (= ", dims(east)[1], "), `north` dim 1 (= ", dims(north)[1], ").");
    if (dims(item_lag)[1] != NI) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_lpdf: dim mismatch — `item_lag` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_lag)[1], ") does not match `NI` (= ", NI, "), inferred from `item_position` dim 1. `NI` sizes: `item_position` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_position)[1], "), `item_lag` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_lag)[1], ").");
    if (dims(state_pattern)[1] != N) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_lpdf: dim mismatch — `state_pattern` dim 1 (= ", dims(state_pattern)[1], ") does not match `N` (= ", N, "), inferred from `pattern_states` dim 1. `N` sizes: `pattern_states` dim 1 (= ", dims(pattern_states)[1], "), `state_pattern` dim 1 (= ", dims(state_pattern)[1], ").");
    return brm_gmrf_vecchia_logdensity(
        field,
        spatial_length,
        temporal_length,
        L,
        east,
        north,
        origin,
        item_ptr,
        item_position,
        item_lag,
        pattern_ptr,
        pattern_states,
        neighbor_ptr,
        neighbor,
        state_pattern,
        M
    );
}
real brm_gmrf_vecchia_logdensity(
    vector field,
    real spatial_length,
    real temporal_length,
    matrix L,
    vector east,
    vector north,
    array[] int origin,
    array[] int item_ptr,
    array[] int item_position,
    vector item_lag,
    array[] int pattern_ptr,
    array[] int pattern_states,
    array[] int neighbor_ptr,
    array[] int neighbor,
    array[] int state_pattern,
    int M
) {
    int C = dims(L)[1];
    int P = dims(east)[1];
    int NT = dims(origin)[1];
    int NI = dims(item_position)[1];
    int N = dims(pattern_states)[1];
    if (dims(L)[2] != C) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_logdensity: dim mismatch — `L` dim 2 (= ", dims(L)[2], ") does not match `C` (= ", C, "), inferred from `L` dim 1. `C` sizes: `L` dim 1 (= ", dims(L)[1], "), `L` dim 2 (= ", dims(L)[2], ").");
    if (dims(north)[1] != P) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_logdensity: dim mismatch — `north` dim 1 (= ", dims(north)[1], ") does not match `P` (= ", P, "), inferred from `east` dim 1. `P` sizes: `east` dim 1 (= ", dims(east)[1], "), `north` dim 1 (= ", dims(north)[1], ").");
    if (dims(item_lag)[1] != NI) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_logdensity: dim mismatch — `item_lag` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_lag)[1], ") does not match `NI` (= ", NI, "), inferred from `item_position` dim 1. `NI` sizes: `item_position` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_position)[1], "), `item_lag` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_lag)[1], ").");
    if (dims(state_pattern)[1] != N) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_logdensity: dim mismatch — `state_pattern` dim 1 (= ", dims(state_pattern)[1], ") does not match `N` (= ", N, "), inferred from `pattern_states` dim 1. `N` sizes: `pattern_states` dim 1 (= ", dims(pattern_states)[1], "), `state_pattern` dim 1 (= ", dims(state_pattern)[1], ").");
    real kappa = (sqrt(2.0) / spatial_length);
    matrix[C, N] z = rep_matrix(0.0, C, N);
    for(s in 1:N) {
        for(c in 1:C) {
            real value = field[(c + (C * (s - 1)))];
            for(k in 1:(c - 1)) {
                value -= (z[k, s] * L[c, k]);
            }
            z[c, s] = (value / L[c, c]);
        }
    }
    real lp = (((-N) * C * log((2.0 * 3.141592653589793))) / 2.0);
    for(c in 1:C) {
        lp -= (N * log(L[c, c]));
    }
    for(p in 1:NT) {
        vector[(M + 1)] weights = brm_gmrf_vecchia_weights(
            p,
            kappa,
            temporal_length,
            east,
            north,
            origin,
            item_ptr,
            item_position,
            item_lag,
            M
        );
        int m = (item_ptr[(p + 1)] - item_ptr[p]);
        real q = 0.0;
        for(slot in pattern_ptr[p]:(pattern_ptr[(p + 1)] - 1)) {
            int s = pattern_states[slot];
            for(c in 1:C) {
                real r = z[c, s];
                for(a in 1:m) {
                    r -= (weights[a] * z[c, neighbor[((neighbor_ptr[s] + a) - 1)]]);
                }
                q += square(r);
            }
        }
        int count = ((pattern_ptr[(p + 1)] - pattern_ptr[p]) * C);
        lp -= (((count * log(weights[(M + 1)])) + (q / weights[(M + 1)])) / 2.0);
    }
    return lp;
}
vector brm_gmrf_vecchia_weights(
    int p,
    real kappa,
    real temporal_length,
    vector east,
    vector north,
    array[] int origin,
    array[] int item_ptr,
    array[] int item_position,
    vector item_lag,
    int M
) {
    int P = dims(east)[1];
    int NI = dims(item_position)[1];
    if (dims(north)[1] != P) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_weights: dim mismatch — `north` dim 1 (= ", dims(north)[1], ") does not match `P` (= ", P, "), inferred from `east` dim 1. `P` sizes: `east` dim 1 (= ", dims(east)[1], "), `north` dim 1 (= ", dims(north)[1], ").");
    if (dims(item_lag)[1] != NI) reject("brm_gmrf_vecchia_weights: dim mismatch — `item_lag` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_lag)[1], ") does not match `NI` (= ", NI, "), inferred from `item_position` dim 1. `NI` sizes: `item_position` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_position)[1], "), `item_lag` dim 1 (= ", dims(item_lag)[1], ").");
    int first_item = item_ptr[p];
    int m = (item_ptr[(p + 1)] - first_item);
    vector[(M + 1)] out = rep_vector(0.0, (M + 1));
    matrix[M, M] A = rep_matrix(0.0, M, M);
    int center = origin[p];
    for(j in 1:m) {
        int pj = item_position[((first_item + j) - 1)];
        real lj = item_lag[((first_item + j) - 1)];
        for(i in j:m) {
            int pk = item_position[((first_item + i) - 1)];
            real lk = item_lag[((first_item + i) - 1)];
            A[i, j] = (
                brm_gmrf_matern1((kappa * hypot((east[pk] - east[pj]), (north[pk] - north[pj])))) *
                exp(((-abs((lk - lj))) / temporal_length))
            );
        }
        out[j] = (
            brm_gmrf_matern1((kappa * hypot((east[center] - east[pj]), (north[center] - north[pj])))) *
            exp(((-abs(lj)) / temporal_length))
        );
    }
    for(j in 1:m) {
        real d = A[j, j];
        for(k in 1:(j - 1)) {
            d -= square(A[j, k]);
        }
        d = sqrt(d);
        A[j, j] = d;
        for(i in (j + 1):m) {
            real value = A[i, j];
            for(k in 1:(j - 1)) {
                value -= (A[i, k] * A[j, k]);
            }
            A[i, j] = (value / d);
        }
    }
    real variance = 1.0;
    for(i in 1:m) {
        real value = out[i];
        for(k in 1:(i - 1)) {
            value -= (A[i, k] * out[k]);
        }
        out[i] = (value / A[i, i]);
        variance -= square(out[i]);
    }
    for(step in 1:m) {
        int i = ((m + 1) - step);
        real value = out[i];
        for(k in (i + 1):m) {
            value -= (A[k, i] * out[k]);
        }
        out[i] = (value / A[i, i]);
    }
    out[(M + 1)] = variance;
    return out;
}
real brm_gmrf_matern1(
    real x
) {
    return ((x > 0.0) ? (x * modified_bessel_second_kind(1, x)) : 1.0);
}
vector normal_lpdfs(
    vector obs,
    vector loc,
    real scale
) {
    return jbroadcasted_normal_lpdfs(obs, loc, scale);
}
vector jbroadcasted_normal_lpdfs(
    vector x1,
    vector x2,
    real x3
) {
    int n = dims(x1)[1];
    vector[n] rv;
    for(i in 1:n) {
        rv[i] = normal_lpdfs(broadcasted_getindex(x1, i), broadcasted_getindex(x2, i), x3);
    }
    return rv;
}
real normal_lpdfs(
    real args1,
    real args2,
    real args3
) {
    return normal_lpdf(args1 | args2, args3);
}
real broadcasted_getindex(vector x, int i) {
    return x[i];
}
vector normal_vector_rng(
    int anontok__1,
    vector a,
    real b
) {
    int n = anontok__1;
    if((n == 0)) {
        vector[n] rv;
        return rv;
    } else {
        return to_vector(normal_rng(a, b));
    }
}
}

The panes show one declaration and its generated backends. The field contributes directly to the predictor; sd is its amplitude, without another population coefficient. Add 1 + gmrf(...) when the model needs an intercept.

Run and diagnose ​

The fit script samples the RK density with WarmupHMC. Each chain gets its own log-density problem, and so its own gradient workspace, and starts with the scalar hyperparameters at their prior medians:

julia
    # One RK log density per chain, prior-median starts, a completion quorum.
    rk = RKBRMI(station_field_model(data))
    backend = AutoEnzyme(; mode=Enzyme.Reverse)
    problems = [rk_logdensity_problem(rk; ad_backend=backend) for _ in 1:n_chains]
    init = [brm_start(rk, (;); base=:prior_median) for _ in problems]
    seconds = @elapsed out = completion_warmup_mcmc(
        [Xoshiro(seed + i) for i in 1:n_chains], problems;
        init, min_completed, n_draws, progress, checkpoint_dir, resume)

The fit runs once, outside the documentation build; this page reads its summaries, and the Reproduce section records the run.

R-hat and effective sample sizes cover all sampler coordinates, using equally long prefixes of the retained chains. The completion quorum can omit slower chains; these diagnostics do not rule out bias from selecting chains by runtime. Inspect divergences and chain agreement before interpreting the maps.

Temporal lengthtime units12623Prior median 4, 95% 1.5–111.00041915801

The noise SD's interval contains its generating value. The generating surface is not a Gaussian process, so the field SD and the two lengths have no true values; compare them with their priors. A long spatial length couples distant stations, and a long temporal length keeps the field similar across nearby times. The data move the temporal length above most of its prior range: each feature moves a few kilometers per time unit, less than its own width. The spatial length stays near its prior median, with a narrower interval.

Read and map the field ​

Sampler coordinates are rows of the draw matrix; posterior draws are columns. Read fitted locations with rk_draw_tree(rk, draws, (:field,)).field, then reduce its named :draw axis with quantile or std from TreeArrays. Raw sampler coordinates are not field values.

For new coordinates and times, brm_gmrf_predict returns one row per point and one column per draw. TreeArrays reduces the named draw axis to the map quantiles:

julia
    # rng adds the conditional uncertainty at locations the fit did not read.
    field_draws = brm_gmrf_predict(rk, draws, :field; east, north, time, rng=Xoshiro(seed))
    field = TreeData(field_draws, :point, :draw)
    bands = quantile(field, (; q025=0.025, q25=0.25, q50=0.5, q75=0.75, q975=0.975); dims=:draw)
    values = map(k -> collect(TreeActualArray(getproperty(bands, k))), (:q025, :q25, :q50, :q75, :q975))
    uncertainty = collect(TreeActualArray(std(field; dims=:draw)))

Passing a random-number generator includes conditional variation at new locations. Without it, the result contains conditional means; their spread understates pointwise uncertainty away from observations.

Dots mark stations; all panels share a color scale.","alt":"Generating field and posterior median at each time. Dots mark stations; all panels share a color scale."}

The posterior median places both features and follows their motion between times. It is shallower than the generating surface in the negative feature at every time, and in the positive feature from time 3 on; the field's prior has mean zero, and the estimate shrinks toward it. Hover over a cell to read its coordinates and value.

The SD is lowest at the stations and about twice as large between them; the checks below give both means. Each new point has its conditional marginal law, but points are drawn independently given the fitted states. These draws support pointwise intervals; they do not supply the joint covariance needed for uncertainty in a spatial total.

The bands show uncertainty at individual locations. They are not simultaneous coverage bands for an entire curve, and predicting a future measurement would also require observation noise.

Checks against the generating surface ​

The truth is known here because the data are synthetic. On the map grid at the three observation times:

Grid checkValue
Grid root mean squared error0.13
Grid points whose 95% interval contains the generating value1320 of 1323
Grid points outside it (time: east, north in km)time 6: (45, 85); time 6: (55, 85); time 6: (55, 90)
Mean field SD, grid points within 5 km of a station0.17
Mean field SD, grid points over 12 km from every station0.32
Draws used for mapping300

All but three grid points' 95% intervals contain the generating value, so on this surface the intervals are wide rather than tight. The three misses lie on the northern edge at time 6, where the generating value sits just above the upper bound. One simulated field is not a calibration study: nearby cells share information, so repeat the simulation across datasets before making a coverage claim. In an application, held-out stations or times check the fit between stations; residuals at the fitted rows do not.

The neighbor count sets a covariance approximation, not the map's resolution, and a denser map grid does not improve it. Refit with more neighbors when conclusions depend on fine spatial structure. A change of representation, mesh or basis also needs a new fit; replay only evaluates the fitted model at new inputs.

For areal counts, smooth channel surfaces, mesh priors and minibatch SVI, see the space-time fields guide.

Reproduce ​

Commands and fit receipt

The repository's test environment supplies the pinned BRM, ReactiveKernels, WarmupHMC and TreeArrays dependencies. These shell commands are manual: the docs build executes the model declaration and the figure code but reads the completed fit's summaries.

sh
julia --startup-file=no --project=test test/setup_env.jl
julia --startup-file=no --project=test research/space_time_fields/fields.jl

The receipt's key hashes the emitted program, the data, the settings, the seed and the harness version. The draws stay outside git, under BRM_DOCS_CACHE (by default a directory below the system temporary directory); a second run with the same key rebuilds the tables from them. A run under a new key within 30 days of the last one needs BRM_DOCS_FIT_FORCE=1.
